Negative Multinomial Family Panel Regression (NM1, NM2, NM-P)

negmultinom.Rd

Estimate a negative multinomial (NM) regression model for clustered or panel count data. Within each cluster (e.g., a site observed over several years), the counts are conditionally independent Poisson variables that share a common gamma-distributed multiplicative frailty with mean 1. Integrating over the frailty gives the negative multinomial likelihood in closed form.

Three members of the family are available, mirroring the NB-1, NB-2, and NB-P forms of the negative binomial in countreg:

  • "NM2" (default): the conventional negative multinomial. Every observation, and every within-cluster aggregate, has an NB-2 marginal with the same \(\alpha\). This is the model estimated by repois.

  • "NM1": the frailty variance is calibrated so that the cluster total follows an NB-1 distribution.

  • "NMP": the frailty variance is calibrated so that the cluster total follows an NB-P distribution with power parameter \(p\).

Both \(\ln(\alpha)\) and \(p\) can be specified as functions of cluster-level variables.

Usage

negmultinom(
  formula,
  group_var,
  data,
  family = "NM2",
  offset = NULL,
  dis_param_formula_1 = NULL,
  dis_param_formula_2 = NULL,
  method = "BFGS",
  max.iters = 1000,
  start.vals = NULL,
  stderr = "normal",
  bootstraps = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

formula

an R formula for the mean, e.g. y ~ x1 + x2. An offset() term may be included in the formula.

group_var

character vector naming the variable(s) that identify the clusters (e.g., a site or panel ID). If more than one variable is given, clusters are defined by their interaction.

data

a data frame containing all variables used in the model.

family

the member of the negative multinomial family to estimate: "NM2" (default), "NM1", or "NMP". Case and non-alphanumeric characters are ignored, so "NM-P" and "nm2" are accepted.

offset

optional character vector naming offset variable(s) in data. Multiple offsets are summed. Do not also use offset() in formula for the same variable.

dis_param_formula_1

optional one-sided formula for \(\ln(\alpha)\), e.g. ~ x3. If NULL, a single constant \(\ln(\alpha)\) is estimated. See Details on within-cluster variation.

dis_param_formula_2

optional one-sided formula for \(p\) (only used when family = "NMP"). The identity link is used, so \(p = W\delta\). If NULL, a single constant \(p\) is estimated.

method

optimization method passed to maxLik. One of "BFGS" (default), "NR", "BHHH", "NM", "CG", "BFGSR", or "SANN". An analytic gradient is supplied to the gradient-based methods.

max.iters

maximum number of iterations for the optimizer.

start.vals

optional numeric vector of starting values, ordered as the mean coefficients, then the \(\ln(\alpha)\) coefficient(s), then (for "NMP") the \(p\) coefficient(s).

stderr

type of standard errors: "normal" (default; inverse of the negative Hessian), "robust" (sandwich estimator using cluster-level scores, i.e., cluster-robust), or "boot" (cluster bootstrap; requires bootstraps).

bootstraps

integer number of cluster bootstrap replications used when stderr = "boot".

verbose

logical. If TRUE, optimizer progress is printed.

Value

An object of class flexCountReg, a list with components:

  • model: the fitted model. Along with the maxLik output, this includes estimate, se, vcov, family, alpha and p (cluster-level values), fitted.values (marginal means \(\mu_{it}\)), eb.fitted (EB expected frequencies), frailty.posterior (cluster posterior mean of \(U_i\)), n_groups, nobs, aic, and bic.

  • data: the data frame used to fit the model.

  • call: the matched call.

  • formula: the formula used to fit the model.

Details

Model structure

Let \(i\) index clusters and \(t\) index the observations within a cluster. The mean is modeled as $$\mu_{it} = \exp(X_{it}\beta + \text{offset}_{it}).$$ Conditional on a cluster frailty \(U_i\), $$Y_{it} \mid U_i \sim \text{Poisson}(\mu_{it} U_i),$$ independently over \(t\), and \(U_i \sim \text{Gamma}(r_i, 1/r_i)\) so that \(E(U_i) = 1\) and \(\text{Var}(U_i) = 1/r_i\).

Define the cluster totals over the reference collection \(R\) (all of a cluster's observations used in estimation): $$y_{iR} = \sum_t y_{it}, \qquad \mu_{iR} = \sum_t \mu_{it}.$$

The three family members differ only in the gamma shape parameter \(r_i\): $$\text{NM2: } r_i = \frac{1}{\alpha_i}, \qquad \text{NM1: } r_i = \frac{\mu_{iR}}{\alpha_i}, \qquad \text{NM-P: } r_i = \frac{\mu_{iR}^{2-p_i}}{\alpha_i}.$$ NM2 and NM1 are the special cases \(p = 2\) and \(p = 1\) of NM-P.

Probability mass function

Integrating over \(U_i\) gives the negative multinomial PMF: $$P(\mathbf{y}_i \mid \boldsymbol{\mu}_i) = \frac{\Gamma(r_i + y_{iR})}{\Gamma(r_i)\prod_t y_{it}!} \left(\frac{r_i}{r_i + \mu_{iR}}\right)^{r_i} \prod_t \left(\frac{\mu_{it}}{r_i + \mu_{iR}}\right)^{y_{it}}.$$

The log-likelihood for cluster \(i\) is: $$LL_i = \ln\Gamma(r_i + y_{iR}) - \ln\Gamma(r_i) + r_i\ln(r_i) - (r_i + y_{iR})\ln(r_i + \mu_{iR}) + \sum_t y_{it}\ln(\mu_{it}) - \sum_t \ln(y_{it}!).$$

Mean and variance

For every family member, \(E(Y_{it}) = \mu_{it}\). The variance and covariance are: $$\text{Var}(Y_{it}) = \mu_{it} + \frac{\mu_{it}^2}{r_i}, \qquad \text{Cov}(Y_{is}, Y_{it}) = \frac{\mu_{is}\mu_{it}}{r_i}.$$ The cluster total therefore satisfies $$\text{Var}(Y_{iR}) = \mu_{iR} + \alpha_i\mu_{iR}^{p_i},$$ i.e., it is NB-2, NB-1, or NB-P for "NM2", "NM1", and "NMP", respectively.

Interpretation of NM1 and NM-P

For NM2, \(r_i = 1/\alpha_i\) does not depend on the mean, so each individual observation (and any within-cluster subtotal) is NB-2 with the same \(\alpha\). The model is coherent across temporal aggregation.

For \(p \neq 2\), the frailty distribution depends on \(\mu_{iR}\). Only the cluster total over the reference collection has the NB-P (or NB-1) variance function; individual observations have \(\text{Var}(Y_{it}) = \mu_{it} + \alpha_i\mu_{iR}^{p_i - 2}\mu_{it}^2\), which is not NB-P with the same \(\alpha\) and \(p\). The reference collection used here is all rows of a cluster that remain after removing missing values. Changing the set of observations in a cluster (e.g., adding or dropping years) changes the implied frailty distribution, so NM1 and NM-P should be interpreted as reference-window-specific joint models.

Parameters as functions of variables

When dis_param_formula_1 or dis_param_formula_2 is supplied, $$\ln(\alpha_i) = \bar{Z}_i\gamma, \qquad p_i = \bar{W}_i\delta,$$ where \(\bar{Z}_i\) and \(\bar{W}_i\) are the within-cluster means of the corresponding design matrices. Because \(\alpha\) and \(p\) describe the shared cluster frailty, they must be constant within a cluster. Cluster-level variables (constant within a cluster) are therefore recommended; if a variable varies within a cluster, a warning is issued and its cluster mean is used.

The \(\ln(\alpha)\) parameters use a log link so that \(\alpha > 0\). The \(p\) parameters use the identity link, so \(p\) is unrestricted.

Empirical Bayes estimates

Given the cluster history, the posterior of the frailty is \(U_i \mid \mathbf{y}_i \sim \text{Gamma}(r_i + y_{iR}, 1/(r_i + \mu_{iR}))\). The returned model includes the empirical Bayes (EB) expected frequency for each observation: $$E(\Lambda_{it} \mid \mathbf{y}_i) = \mu_{it}\frac{r_i + y_{iR}}{r_i + \mu_{iR}}.$$ For NM2 this is \(\mu_{it}(1 + \alpha y_{iR})/(1 + \alpha\mu_{iR})\). EB estimates for new data can be obtained with predict(model, newdata, method = "EB") when newdata contains the outcome and grouping variables.

Standard errors

The log-likelihood is evaluated cluster by cluster, so the "robust" sandwich estimator and the "BHHH" optimizer both use cluster-level scores. The bootstrap resamples whole clusters.

References

Cameron, A. C., & Trivedi, P. K. (2013). Regression Analysis of Count Data (2nd ed.). Cambridge University Press.

Greene, W. (2008). Functional forms for the negative binomial model for count data. Economics Letters, 99(3), 585-590.

Hausman, J., Hall, B. H., & Griliches, Z. (1984). Econometric models for count data with an application to the patents-R&D relationship. Econometrica, 52(4), 909-938.

See also

repois, countreg, predict.flexCountReg

Examples

# \donttest{
data("washington_roads")
washington_roads$AADTover10k <- ifelse(washington_roads$AADT > 10000, 1, 0)

# Conventional negative multinomial (NM2)
nm2 <- negmultinom(Animal ~ lnaadt + speed50 + ShouldWidth04 + AADTover10k,
                   group_var = "ID", data = washington_roads,
                   offset = "lnlength")
summary(nm2)
